reason: The cited evidence directly supports all key premises: it demonstrates HfO2 formation, reduced weight gain, and prevention of surface degradation for a coated VZrHfNbTa alloy under the specified conditions. The mechanism of oxygen diffusion barrier is implied by the dense HfO2 layer and improved resistance. The evidence is accurately represented without overstatement.
premises: A hafnium-rich coating on VZrHfNbTa forms a dense HfO2 protective layer during high-temperature oxidation.
The HfO2 layer acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen, limiting oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The coated alloy shows significantly reduced weight gain compared to the uncoated alloy.
The coating prevents surface degradation such as denting and pulverization.
The coating is effective in air at around 1000°C for prolonged periods.
